units.zh: 《易》稱「遯之時義大矣哉」。
units.en: The Book of Changes says, "In the hour of Withdrawal, the meaning of timing is vast indeed."
units.literal: The Changes states, "The timely significance of the hexagram Dun (Withdrawal) is great indeed."

units.zh: 又曰：“不事王侯，高尚其事。”
units.en: It adds, "They will not wait on lords and princes; they exalt their own calling instead."
units.literal: It also says, "They do not serve kings and marquises; they make lofty their own undertakings."

units.zh: 是以尧称则天，不屈颍阳之高；
units.en: So Yao could mirror Heaven and still leave the recluses of Yingyang untroubled in their height;
units.literal: Therefore Yao was said to pattern himself on Heaven, yet he did not bend the height of those at Yingyang;

units.zh: 武尽美矣，终全孤竹之洁。
units.en: King Wu won perfect renown, yet he still spared the stainless recluses of Mount Guzhu.
units.literal: King Wu was utterly admirable, yet in the end he preserved the purity of those of Guzhu.

units.zh: 自兹以降，风流弥繁，长往之轨未殊，而感致之数匪一。
units.en: Afterward the tradition only spread: the path of withdrawal stayed one, but the motives that led men to it multiplied.
units.literal: From this time downward, the current of such conduct grew ever richer; the track of those who went far away was not different, yet the ways they were moved and brought to it were not one.

units.zh: 或隐居以求其志，或回避以全其道，或静已以镇其躁，或去危以图其安，或垢俗以动其概，或疵物以激其清。
units.en: Some hid to pursue a purpose; some fled to keep the Way intact; some stilled themselves against inner hurry; some quit peril for safety; some smeared themselves in the mire to steel their honor; some scorned the world to sharpen their cleanness.
units.literal: Some concealed themselves in order to seek their aims; some withdrew in order to preserve their Way; some quieted themselves to still their restlessness; some left danger to plan their safety; some befouled themselves amid vulgarity to rouse their integrity; some faulted things to quicken their purity.

units.zh: 然观其甘心畎亩之中，憔悴江海之上，岂必亲鱼鸟、乐林草哉！
units.en: Yet see them content in plowed fields, worn thin along the rivers—surely it was not only love of birds, fish, and wild growth!
units.literal: Yet observe how they were willing to remain in the furrows of the fields, haggard upon the rivers and seas—was it surely that they had to fondle fish and birds and delight in woods and grass!

units.zh: 亦云性分所至而已。
units.en: They were simply following the grain of their own natures, nothing more.
units.literal: One may also say it reached what their nature and allotment decreed, that is all.

units.zh: 故蒙耻之宾，屡黜不去其国；
units.en: Thus men who swallowed humiliation might be cast out again and again yet never quit their homeland;
units.literal: Therefore guests who bore shame were repeatedly dismissed yet did not leave their states;

units.zh: 蹈海之节，千乘莫移其情。
units.en: while others who chose the sea's integrity could not be moved by the offer of a thousand chariots.
units.literal: those who trod the integrity of leaping into the sea—no state of a thousand chariots could shift their resolve.

units.zh: 适使矫易去就，则不能相为矣。
units.en: Had you forced them to swap places, none could have stood in another's stead.
units.literal: Had they been forced to twist their choices of staying or going, they could not have acted for one another.

units.zh: 彼虽硁硁有类沽名者，然而蝉蜕嚣埃之中，自致寰区之外，异夫饰智巧以逐浮利者乎！
units.en: A few may look stiff-necked, almost like fame-hunters, yet they shed the world's racket and walk outside its borders—far from the clever types angling for hollow gain.
units.literal: Though they may seem rigidly narrow, resembling reputation-mongers, yet they slough off the clamor of dust and place themselves beyond the realm—how different from those who polish cleverness to chase floating profit!

units.zh: 荀卿有言曰，“志意修则骄富贵，道义重则轻王公”也。
units.en: Xunzi said, "Refine your intent and you scorn riches and rank; weight your conduct with the Way and you think little of kings and princes."
units.literal: Xun Qing had a saying: "When one's aims and thoughts are cultivated, one is proud toward wealth and honor; when the Way and righteousness weigh heavily, one is light toward kings and dukes."

units.zh: 汉室中微，王莽篡位，士之蕴藉义愤甚矣。
units.en: Mid-Han faltered, Wang Mang seized the throne, and every scholar's breast burned with loyal rage.
units.literal: The house of Han waned in its middle period; Wang Mang usurped the throne, and gentlemen of learning nursed righteous indignation to an extreme degree.

units.zh: 是时裂冠毁冕，相携持而去之者，盖不可胜数。
units.en: Then came the wave who rent their caps and crowns and marched away together—no reckoning could count them.
units.literal: At that time those who tore caps and shattered coronets and, hand in hand, departed could not be counted.

units.zh: 杨雄曰：“鸿飞冥冥，弋者何篡焉。”
units.en: Yang Xiong wrote, "The wild goose vanishes into the gloom—what can the fowler's string catch?"
units.literal: Yang Xiong said, "The swan flies into the dark depths; what can the archer's string snare?"

units.zh: 言其违患之远也。
units.en: —meaning how far they flew from harm.
units.literal: This speaks of how far they kept from calamity.

units.zh: 光武侧席幽人，求之若不及，旌帛蒲车之所征贲，相望于岩中矣。
units.en: Guangwu turned his mat for hidden men and hunted them as if always a step behind—silk summons and rush-wheeled coaches thickly threaded the cliffs.
units.literal: Emperor Guangwu set aside a seat for recluses and sought them as if he could not catch up; the silken banners and rush-wheeled coaches that summoned and honored them were visible one after another in the mountain valleys.

units.zh: 若薛方、逢萌，聘而不肯至；
units.en: Xue Fang and Feng Meng were called but would not appear;
units.literal: Such men as Xue Fang and Feng Meng were summoned yet were unwilling to come;

units.zh: 严光、周党、王霸，至而不能屈。
units.en: Yan Guang, Zhou Dang, and Wang Ba came yet could not be bowed.
units.literal: Yan Guang, Zhou Dang, and Wang Ba came yet could not be bent.

units.zh: 群方咸遂，志士怀仁，斯固所谓“举逸民天下归心”者乎！
units.en: Each found his path, and high-minded men kept faith with humaneness—was this not the "raise the recluses and all hearts incline" of the Analects?
units.literal: The many regions all had their fulfillment; men of high purpose cherished humaneness—was this not indeed what is called "Raise up withdrawn men and the realm will turn its heart to you"?

units.zh: 肃宗亦礼郑均而征高凤，以成其节。
units.en: Emperor Zhang likewise honored Zheng Jun and summoned Gao Feng to crown their resolve.
units.literal: Emperor Su also honored Zheng Jun with ritual and summoned Gao Feng, thereby completing their integrity.

units.zh: 自后帝德稍衰，邪孽当朝，处子耿介，羞与卿相等列，至乃抗愤而不顾，多失其中行焉。
units.en: Later the throne's virtue thinned, vicious favorites ruled the hall, and hermits—too proud to sit among ministers—sometimes flamed into defiance and lost the golden mean.
units.literal: Afterward imperial virtue gradually declined; evil favorites held the court, gentlemen-recluses stood stiffly aloof, ashamed to rank with ministers and grandees, until some flared in defiance and recklessly missed the middle course.

units.zh: 盖录其绝尘不反，同夫作者，列之此篇。
units.en: Here I record those who shook off the dust and never looked back—true authors of their own lives—and set them in this scroll.
units.literal: Therefore I record those who cut off the dust and never returned, peers of the makers of texts, and array them in this chapter.

units.zh: 高鳳
units.en: Gao Feng
units.literal: Gao Feng

units.zh: 野王二老者
units.en: The two old men of Yewang
units.literal: The two old men of Yewang

units.zh: 野王二老者，不知何许人也。
units.en: No one knows where the two elders of Yewang came from.
units.literal: The two old men of Yewang—no one knows what place they were from.

units.zh: 初，光武贰于更始，会关中扰乱，遣前将军邓禹西征，送之于道。
units.en: When Guangwu still hedged toward Gengshi and Guanzhong boiled, he sent Forward General Deng Yu west and escorted him along the road.
units.literal: In the beginning, when Guangwu was of two minds toward Emperor Gengshi, there happened turmoil in the Guanzhong region; he dispatched Forward General Deng Yu on a western expedition and saw him off along the road.

units.zh: 既反，因于野王猎，路见二老者即禽。
units.en: On the return hunt at Yewang he met two greybeards about to shoot game.
units.literal: Having turned back, he therefore hunted at Yewang on the way and, on the road, saw two old men about to take game.

units.zh: 光武问曰：“禽何向？”
units.en: Guangwu asked, "Which way lies the quarry?"
units.literal: Guangwu asked, saying, "In what direction is the game?"

units.zh: 并举手西指，言“此中多虎，臣每即禽，虎亦即臣，大王勿往也。”
units.en: Both pointed west: "Tigers swarm there—we hunt them, they hunt us—do not ride that way, great king."
units.literal: Together they raised their hands and pointed west, saying, "In here there are many tigers; we each time take game, and the tigers also each time take us—great king, do not go there."

units.zh: 光武曰：“苟有其备，虎亦何患。”
units.en: Guangwu said, "With proper precautions, what fear of tigers?"
units.literal: Guangwu said, "If one has preparations for it, what worry have tigers?"

units.zh: 父曰：“何大王之谬邪！
units.en: The elder answered, "How wrong you are, great king!
units.literal: The elder said, "How mistaken is the great king!

units.zh: 昔汤即桀于鸣条，而大城于亳；
units.en: Tang seized Jie at Mingtiao, then raised mighty ramparts at Bo;
units.literal: In antiquity Tang took Jie at Mingtiao, yet built a great wall at Bo;

units.zh: 武王亦即纣于牧野，而大城于郏鄏。
units.en: King Wu struck Zhou at Muye, then ringed Jiaru with great walls.
units.literal: King Wu likewise took Zhou at Muye, yet built a great wall at Jiaru.

units.zh: 彼二王者，其备非不深也。
units.en: Neither king lacked deep defenses.
units.literal: Those two kings—their preparations were not shallow.

units.zh: 是以即人者，人亦即之，虽有其备，庸可忽乎！”
units.en: He who hunts men is hunted in turn—how can you trust walls alone?"
units.literal: Therefore those who seize others are also seized by others; though they have preparations, how can they be treated lightly!"

units.zh: 光武悟其旨，顾左右曰：“此隐者也。”
units.en: Guangwu understood and murmured to his attendants, "These are hidden sages."
units.literal: Guangwu grasped their intent, looked to those at his left and right, and said, "These are recluses."

units.zh: 将用之，辞而去，莫知所在。
units.en: He moved to retain them, but they slipped away—none traced their path.
units.literal: He was about to employ them, but they declined and departed; no one knew where they went.

units.zh: 向长字子平，河内朝歌人也。
units.en: Xiang Chang, styled Ziping, came from Zhaoge in Henei.
units.literal: Xiang Chang, courtesy name Ziping, was a man of Zhaoge in Henei.

units.zh: 隐居不仕，性尚中和，好通《老》、《易》。
units.en: He lived in reclusion, prized equipoise, and loved plumbing the Laozi and the Changes.
units.literal: He concealed himself and did not take office; by nature he esteemed centrality and harmony and loved to penetrate the Laozi and the Changes.

units.zh: 贫无资食，好事者更馈焉，受之取足而反其余。
units.en: Destitute, he lived on neighbors' gifts—taking only what he needed and sending the rest back.
units.literal: Poor, without means for food, well-wishers alternately sent gifts; he accepted only enough to suffice and returned the remainder.

units.zh: 王莽大司空王邑辟之，连年乃至，欲荐之于莽，固辞乃止。
units.en: Wang Mang's grand minister Wang Yi summoned him; he dragged his feet for years, and when Yi tried to push him at court he refused point-blank.
units.literal: Grand Minister of Works under Wang Mang, Wang Yi, summoned him; only after successive years did he arrive; Yi wished to recommend him to Mang, but he firmly declined and only then stopped.

units.zh: 潜隐于家。
units.en: He sank from sight in his own house.
units.literal: He hid away at home.

units.zh: 读《易》至《损》、《益》卦，喟然叹曰：“吾已知富不如贫，贵不如贱，但未知死何如生耳。”
units.en: At the Sun and Yi hexagrams he sighed, "I know wealth cannot beat poverty nor rank a humble station—but how death stacks against life I cannot tell."
units.literal: Reading the Changes to the hexagrams Sun and Yi, he sighed with feeling and said, "I already know that wealth is not as good as poverty, honor not as good as low status, but I still do not know how death compares to life."

units.zh: 建武中，男女娶嫁既毕，敕断家事勿相关，当如我死也。
units.en: In the Jianwu years, once his children were wed, he commanded the household to treat him as dead and ask nothing of him.
units.literal: In the Jianwu era, when the marrying of his sons and daughters was finished, he ordered that domestic affairs should no longer concern one another, as if he had died.

units.zh: 于是遂肆意，与同好北海禽庆俱游五岳名山，竟不知所终。
units.en: Then he wandered at will with his friend Qin Qing of Beihai across the five sacred peaks until both vanished from record.
units.literal: Thereupon he followed his whim and, together with his like-minded friend Qin Qing of Beihai, roamed the five marchmounts and famous mountains, and in the end no one knew his final end.

units.zh: 逢萌字子康，北海都昌人也。
units.en: Feng Meng, styled Zikang, was a native of Duchang in Beihai.
units.literal: Feng Meng, courtesy name Zikang, was a man of Duchang in Beihai.

units.zh: 家贫，给事县为亭长。
units.en: His home was humble; he clerked as a village headman.
units.literal: His family was poor; he served the county as village headman.

units.zh: 时尉行过亭，萌候迎拜谒，既而掷楯叹曰：“大丈夫安能为人役哉！”
units.en: When the commandant passed his post, Feng greeted him, then hurled down his station shield and cried, "A grown man cannot be another man's hireling!"
units.literal: At the time the commandant was passing the post station; Meng waited, welcomed, and bowed in audience, then cast aside his shield and sighed, saying, "How can a great man be another's servant!"

units.zh: 遂去之长安学，通《春秋经》。
units.en: He left for the capital, studied, and mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals.
units.literal: Thereupon he left for Chang'an to study and mastered the Spring and Autumn classic.

units.zh: 时王莽杀其子宇，萌谓友人曰：“三纲绝矣！
units.en: When Wang Mang murdered his own son Yu, Feng told a friend, "The three cardinal ties are cut!
units.literal: At the time Wang Mang had killed his son Yu; Meng said to a friend, "The three bonds are snapped!

units.zh: 不去，祸将及人。”
units.en: Stay, and calamity will swallow us all."
units.literal: If we do not leave, disaster will reach people."

units.zh: 即解冠挂东都城门，归，将家属浮海，客于辽东。
units.en: He hung his cap on the eastern capital gate, fled home, and sailed his family to Liaodong.
units.literal: He immediately doffed his cap and hung it on the east gate of the capital, returned, and took his household floating on the sea, sojourning in Liaodong.

units.zh: 萌素明阴阳，知莽将败，有顷，乃首戴瓦盎，哭于市曰：“新乎新乎！”
units.en: Feng read the omens: seeing Mang's fall, he soon walked the market with an earthen bowl on his head, wailing, "New! New!"
units.literal: Meng by nature understood yin and yang; knowing that Mang would fall, before long he then first put a clay bowl on his head and wept in the market, saying, "New! New!"

units.zh: 因遂潜藏。
units.en: —then dropped from sight.
units.literal: Thereupon he hid himself away.

units.zh: 及光武即位，乃之琅邪劳山，养志修道，人皆化其德。
units.en: When Guangwu rose, Feng withdrew to Mount Lao in Langye, nursed his purpose, and won every neighbor by his virtue.
units.literal: When Guangwu took the throne, he then went to Mount Lao in Langye, nurtured his aims and cultivated the Way, and people were all transformed by his virtue.

units.zh: 北海太守素闻其高，遣吏奉谒致礼，萌不答。
units.en: The Beihai prefect, hearing of his fame, sent a clerk with gifts; Feng never replied.
units.literal: The grand administrator of Beihai had long heard of his loftiness and sent a clerk with a formal visit and gifts; Meng did not answer.

units.zh: 太守怀恨而使捕之。
units.en: The prefect, stung, ordered his arrest.
units.literal: The grand administrator harbored resentment and therefore sent men to seize him.

units.zh: 吏叩头曰：“子康大贤，天下共闻，所在之处，人敬如父，往必不获，只自毁辱。”
units.en: The clerk kowtowed: "All the world honors Zikang as a father—send us and we fail, only earning shame."
units.literal: The clerk knocked his head and said, "Zikang is a great worthy; the whole realm has heard of him; wherever he is, people revere him as a father; if you go you are sure not to obtain him—you will only destroy and shame yourself."

units.zh: 太守怒，收之系狱，更发它吏。
units.en: The prefect jailed the messenger and sent another.
units.literal: The grand administrator was angry, arrested him, and bound him in prison, then sent out another clerk.

units.zh: 行至劳山，人果相率以兵弩捍御。
units.en: At Mount Lao the villagers ringed Feng with bows to shield him.
units.literal: When they reached Mount Lao, the people indeed banded together and with bows and crossbows defended him.

units.zh: 吏被伤流血，奔而还。
units.en: The officers fled bloodied.
units.literal: The clerks were wounded and bleeding, and ran back.

units.zh: 后诏书征萌，托以老耄，迷路东西，语使者云：“朝廷所以征我者，以其有益于政，尚不知方面所在，安能济时乎？”
units.en: Later an imperial summons caught him; he pleaded senility, pretended to wander lost, and told the envoy, "If the court wants my counsel, it should notice I cannot find my own doorstep—how may I save the age?"
units.literal: Later an edict summoned Meng; he pleaded old age and senility, lost his way east and west, and said to the envoy, "The reason the court summons me is that I would benefit governance; I still do not know in what quarter I am—how can I aid the times?"

units.zh: 即便驾归。
units.en: Then he whipped his cart home.
units.literal: Immediately he drove his carriage home.

units.zh: 连征不起，以寿终。
units.en: Further calls failed; he died in old age.
units.literal: Summoned repeatedly, he did not rise; he ended his years by natural lifespan.

units.zh: 初，萌与同郡徐房、平原李子云、王君公相友善，并晓阴阳，怀德秽行。
units.en: Feng had been close to Xu Fang, Li Ziyun, and Wang Jungong—fellow students of yin-yang who prized virtue over reputation.
units.literal: In the beginning Meng was on good terms with Xu Fang of his commandery, Li Ziyun of Pingyuan, and Wang Jungong, all understanding yin and yang and cherishing virtue while keeping their conduct base in the world's eyes.

units.zh: 房与子云养徒各千人，君公遭乱独不去，侩牛自隐。
units.en: Xu and Li each taught a thousand pupils; Wang alone stayed through the chaos, hiding as a cattle broker.
units.literal: Fang and Ziyun each kept disciples to the number of a thousand; Jungong, encountering turmoil, alone did not leave, but brokered oxen to conceal himself.

units.zh: 时人谓之论曰：“避世墙东王君公。”
units.en: Wits rhymed, "East of the wall, avoiding the age, stands Wang Jungong."
units.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: "Wang Jungong east of the wall, avoiding the age."

units.zh: 周党字伯况，太原广武人也。
units.en: Zhou Dang, styled Bokuang, came from Guangwu in Taiyuan.
units.literal: Zhou Dang, courtesy name Bokuang, was a man of Guangwu in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 家产千金。
units.en: His clan owned a fortune in gold.
units.literal: His household property amounted to a thousand in gold.

units.zh: 少孤，为宗人所养，而遇之不以理，及长，又不还其财。
units.en: Orphaned young, he was raised by kinsmen who robbed him; grown, they still refused his inheritance.
units.literal: In his youth he was orphaned; he was reared by lineage kin, yet they did not treat him according to principle, and when he grew, they also did not return his property.

units.zh: 党诣乡县讼，主乃归之。
units.en: He sued in county and commandery until the chief kin relented and restored his share.
units.literal: Dang went to the county and commandery to sue; the head of the lineage then returned it to him.

units.zh: 既而散与宗族，悉免遣奴婢，遂至长安游学。
units.en: He then scattered the wealth to kin, freed every bondservant, and rode to Chang'an to study.
units.literal: Thereupon he distributed it to the lineage kin, entirely manumitted and sent away his male and female slaves, and proceeded to Chang'an to roam-study.

units.zh: 初，乡佐尝众中辱党，党久怀之。
units.en: A village aide had once shamed him in public, and Zhou nursed the grudge.
units.literal: In the beginning a village aide had once humiliated Dang in a crowd; Dang long harbored it.

units.zh: 后读《春秋》，闻复仇之义，便辍讲而还，与乡佐相闻，期克斗日。
units.en: Reading the Spring and Autumn he learned the right of blood feud, broke off classes, challenged the aide, and fixed a duel day.
units.literal: Later, reading the Spring and Autumn, when he heard the righteousness of vengeance for wrongs, he stopped his lectures and returned, communicated with the village aide, and set a day for decisive combat.

units.zh: 既交刃，而党为乡佐所伤，困顿。
units.en: In the fight Zhou fell badly wounded.
units.literal: After they had crossed blades, Dang was wounded by the village aide and was in extremity.

units.zh: 乡佐服其义，舆归养之，数日方苏，既悟而去。
units.en: The aide, awed, carried him home, nursed him until he woke, then Zhou slipped away.
units.literal: The village aide submitted to his righteousness, carried him in a litter home to nurse him, and after several days he revived; once conscious, he departed.

units.zh: 自此敕身修志，州里称其高。
units.en: After that he schooled himself, and the canton hailed his nobility.
units.literal: From this he disciplined himself and cultivated his purpose; the district praised his loftiness.

units.zh: 及王莽窃位，托疾杜门。
units.en: When Wang Mang seized the throne, Zhou feigned sickness and barred his gate.
units.literal: When Wang Mang stole the throne, he pleaded illness and shut his gate.

units.zh: 自后贼暴从横，残灭郡县，唯至广武，过城不入。
units.en: Later rebels ravaged commanderies, yet at Guangwu they marched past without entering.
units.literal: Afterward bandits and violence ran rampant and exterminated commanderies and counties; only when they reached Guangwu did they pass the city and not enter.

units.zh: 建武中，征为议郎，以病去职，遂将妻子居黾池。
units.en: Jianwu brought a summons as remonstrance official; pleading illness he quit and moved his household to Mianchi.
units.literal: In the Jianwu era he was summoned as remonstrance official; because of illness he left office, and therefore led his wife and children to dwell at Mianchi.

units.zh: 复被征，不得已，乃着短布单衣，穀皮绡头，待见尚书。
units.en: Called again, he donned rough cloth, a bark-fiber kerchief, and presented himself to the masters of writing.
units.literal: He was summoned again; having no choice, he then put on short cloth unlined garments, a husk-silk head-wrap, and waited to see the secretary.

units.zh: 及光武引见，党伏而不谒，自陈愿守所志，帝乃许焉。
units.en: Before Guangwu he lay flat and refused the court bow, begging to keep his reclusive vow; the emperor allowed it.
units.literal: When Guangwu granted him audience, Dang lay prostrate and did not perform the obeisance, stating himself that he wished to keep to his resolve, and the emperor thereupon granted it.

units.zh: 博士范升奏毁党曰：“臣闻尧不须许由、巢父，而建号天下；
units.en: Erudite Fan Sheng attacked him: "Yao needed neither Xu You nor Chao Father to rule the world;
units.literal: Erudite Fan Sheng memorialized to attack Dang, saying, "Your servant has heard that Yao did not need Xu You and Chao Fu yet established his title over the realm;

units.zh: 周不待伯夷、叔齐，而王道以成。
units.en: Zhou needed neither Bo Yi nor Shu Qi to perfect the royal Way.
units.literal: Zhou did not wait for Bo Yi and Shu Qi, yet the kingly Way was thereby accomplished.

units.zh: 伏见太原周党、东海王良、山阳王成等，蒙受厚恩，使者三聘，乃肯就车。
units.en: Yet Taiyuan's Zhou Dang, Donghai's Wang Liang, and Shanyang's Wang Cheng soaked up imperial grace and only mounted the coach after three embassies.
units.literal: Your servant has seen Taiyuan's Zhou Dang, Donghai's Wang Liang, Shanyang's Wang Cheng, and others who received deep favor—only after envoys thrice summoned them were they willing to mount the carriage.

units.zh: 及陛见帝廷，党不以礼屈，伏而不谒，偃蹇骄悍，同时俱逝。
units.en: At court they sprawled without bowing—proud, rude, and gone together.
units.literal: When they ascended the hall to be granted audience at the imperial court, Dang did not yield in ritual, lay prostrate and did not perform the obeisance, were arrogant and fierce, and at the same time all departed.

units.zh: 党等文不能演义，武不能死君，钓采华名，庶几三公之位。
units.en: They wield neither brush nor blade for the throne—only angle for empty fame and dream of the three excellencies.
units.literal: Dang and the others in letters could not unfold doctrine; in arms they could not die for their lord; they angle for a flowery name, hoping perchance for the rank of the three dukes.

units.zh: 臣愿与坐云台之下，考试图国之道。
units.en: Let me sit them beneath the Cloud Terrace and test their statecraft.
units.literal: Your servant wishes to sit with them beneath the Cloud Terrace and examine them on the arts of ordering the state.

units.zh: 不如臣言，伏虚妄之罪。
units.en: If I lie, I accept the charge of slander.
units.literal: If they are not as your servant says, let them suffer the crime of empty falsehood.

units.zh: 而敢私窃虚名，夸上求高，皆大不敬。”
units.en: Privately trading on hollow renown to dazzle the throne is grave disrespect."
units.literal: Yet daring privately to steal empty reputation, boasting to the ruler to seek height—all is great irreverence."

units.zh: 书奏，天子以示公卿。
units.en: The emperor circulated Fan's memorial among the high ministers.
units.literal: When the memorial was presented, the Son of Heaven showed it to the dukes and ministers.

units.zh: 诏曰：“自古明王圣主，必有不宾之士。
units.en: The edict read, "Every wise king has guests who refuse to bend.
units.literal: An edict stated, "From antiquity enlightened kings and sage lords have surely had guests who would not submit.

units.zh: 伯夷、叔齐不食周粟，太原周党不受朕禄，亦各有志焉。
units.en: Bo Yi and Shu Qi spurned Zhou grain; Taiyuan's Zhou Dang spurns our stipend—each follows his star.
units.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi would not eat Zhou grain; Taiyuan's Zhou Dang will not accept Our salary—each has his resolve.

units.zh: 其赐帛四十匹。”
units.en: Gift him forty bolts of silk."
units.literal: We grant him forty bolts of silk."

units.zh: 党遂隐居黾池，著书上下篇而终。
units.en: Zhou Dang hid at Mianchi, wrote a two-part book, and died.
units.literal: Dang thereupon concealed himself at Mianchi, wrote a book in upper and lower fascicles, and ended.

units.zh: 邑人贤而祠之。
units.en: His townsfolk judged him worthy and built him a shrine.
units.literal: The people of his town thought him worthy and sacrificed to him.

units.zh: 初，党与同郡谭贤伯升、雁门殷谟君长，俱守节不仕王莽世。
units.en: Zhou, together with Tan Xian, styled Bosheng, of his commandery and Yin Mo, styled Junzhang, of Yanmen, all kept their integrity and refused office under Wang Mang.
units.literal: In the beginning Dang, together with his fellow townsman Tan Xian Borsheng and Yin Mo Junzhang of Yanmen, all kept their integrity and did not take office in Wang Mang's age.

units.zh: 建武中，征，并不到。
units.en: During the Jianwu era, all three men were summoned, but none appeared.
units.literal: During the Jianwu era, all three were summoned, but none came.

units.zh: 王霸字儒仲，太原广武人也。
units.en: Wang Ba, styled Ruzhong, came from Guangwu in Taiyuan.
units.literal: Wang Ba, courtesy name Ruzhong, was a man of Guangwu in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 少有清节。
units.en: From youth he kept his conduct stainless.
units.literal: In his youth he had pure integrity.

units.zh: 及王莽篡位，弃冠带，绝交宦。
units.en: When Wang Mang seized the throne he shed cap and sash and broke with every official tie.
units.literal: When Wang Mang usurped the throne, he cast away cap and belt and cut off association with office-holders.

units.zh: 建武中，征到尚书，拜称名，不称臣。
units.en: Summoned in Jianwu to the masters of writing, he used his personal name in court and refused the title "your subject."
units.literal: In the Jianwu era he was summoned and reached the masters of writing; in audience he gave his personal name and did not call himself 'subject.'

units.zh: 有司问其故。
units.en: The clerks demanded an explanation.
units.literal: The responsible officials asked him the reason.

units.zh: 霸曰：“天子有所不臣，诸侯有所不友。”
units.en: Wang Ba answered, "Even the Son of Heaven has men he will not own as ministers; even lords have men they will not claim as friends."
units.literal: Ba said, "The Son of Heaven has those whom he does not treat as subjects; the feudal lords have those whom they do not treat as friends."

units.zh: 司徒侯霸让位于霸。
units.en: Hou Ba, the Minister of Education, offered to yield his office to Wang Ba.
units.literal: Hou Ba, the Minister of Education, offered to yield his office to Wang Ba.

units.zh: 阎阳毁之曰：“太原俗党，儒仲颇有其风。”
units.en: Yan Yang smeared him: "Taiyuan loves cliques, and Ruzhong reeks of it."
units.literal: Yan Yang slandered him, saying, "Taiyuan is vulgar in cliquishness, and Ruzhong has quite a bit of that wind."

units.zh: 遂止。
units.en: The matter was consequently dropped.
units.literal: Thereupon it stopped.

units.zh: 以病归，隐居守志，茅屋蓬户。
units.en: Pleading illness he went home to a rush gate and thatched roof, guarding his vow.
units.literal: Because of illness he returned home, concealed himself and kept his resolve, with a thatched hut and a door of woven rushes.

units.zh: 连征，不至，以寿终。
units.en: He was repeatedly summoned but never appeared, and eventually died at an advanced age.
units.literal: Summoned repeatedly, he did not come; he ended his years by natural lifespan.

units.zh: 严光字子陵，一名遵，会稽余姚人也。
units.en: Yan Guang, styled Ziling—also called Yan Zun—hailed from Yuyao in Kuaiji.
units.literal: Yan Guang, courtesy name Ziling, also named Zun, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.

units.zh: 少有高名，与光武同游学。
units.en: In youth he was already famous and studied abroad with the future Guangwu.
units.literal: In his youth he had a lofty reputation and roamed-study together with Guangwu.

units.zh: 及光武即位，乃变名姓，隐身不见。
units.en: When his friend became emperor, Yan changed his name and vanished from sight.
units.literal: When Guangwu took the throne, he then changed his name and surname and concealed himself so as not to appear.

units.zh: 帝思其贤，乃令以物色访之。
units.en: The emperor missed his virtue and sent agents to hunt him by description.
units.literal: The emperor thought on his worthiness and therefore ordered him sought by likeness of appearance.

units.zh: 后齐国上言：“有一男子，披羊裘钓泽中。”
units.en: Qi commandery later reported a man in sheepskin angling in the reeds.
units.literal: Later Qi commandery reported upward, "There is one man, draped in sheepskin, fishing in a marsh."

units.zh: 帝疑其光，乃备安车玄纁，遣使聘之。
units.en: Guangwu guessed it was Yan Guang and sent a cushioned coach and black silk to fetch him.
units.literal: The emperor suspected it was Guang and therefore prepared a comfortable carriage and dark silk and dispatched an envoy to summon him.

units.zh: 三反而后至。
units.en: The envoy went back and forth three times before he came.
units.literal: After three returns he then arrived.

units.zh: 舍于北军。
units.en: They quartered him in the Northern Army camp.
units.literal: He lodged at the Northern Army.

units.zh: 给床褥，太官朝夕进膳。
units.en: The court gave him a bed and daily meals from the imperial kitchen.
units.literal: They supplied bedding; morning and evening the grand provisioner advanced meals.

units.zh: 司徒侯霸与光素旧，遣使奉书。
units.en: Minister Hou Ba, an old friend, sent a letter by courier.
units.literal: Minister of Education Hou Ba was of old friendship with Guang and sent a messenger bearing a letter.

units.zh: 使人因谓光曰：“公闻先生至，区区欲即诣造。
units.en: The courier said, "His Lordship burns to call on you at once.
units.literal: The messenger therefore said to Guang, "The lord has heard that the master has arrived; in utmost earnestness he wishes immediately to come pay a visit.

units.zh: 迫于典司，是以不获。
units.en: Duty chains him—he cannot slip away.
units.literal: Pressed by the duties of his office, he therefore cannot obtain it.

units.zh: 愿因日暮，自屈语言。”
units.en: He begs the favor of a twilight talk."
units.literal: He hopes, relying on dusk's falling, humbly to bend himself to converse in words."

units.zh: 光不答，乃投札与之，口授曰：“君房足下：位至鼎足，甚善。
units.en: Yan said nothing, tossed Hou a scrap, and dictated: "Junfang, you stand as one leg of the ruling tripod—well done.
units.literal: Guang did not answer but cast a slip to him and orally dictated, saying, "Sir Junfang, at your feet: your position has reached the tripod's third leg—very good.

units.zh: 怀仁辅义天下悦，阿谀顺旨要领绝。”
units.en: Nourish benevolence and aid the right, and the world smiles; flatter power and your throat meets the blade."
units.literal: Cherish humaneness and assist righteousness and the realm rejoices; flatter and follow orders and your neck will be severed."

units.zh: 霸得书，封奏之。
units.en: Hou sealed the note and forwarded it to the throne.
units.literal: When Ba received the letter, he sealed and memorialized it.

units.zh: 帝笑曰：“狂奴故态也。”
units.en: The emperor laughed, "There is the wild friend I remember."
units.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "The mad servant's old manner."

units.zh: 车驾即日幸其馆。
units.en: That day the imperial carriage rolled to his door.
units.literal: That very day the imperial carriage visited his lodging.

units.zh: 光卧不起，帝即其卧所，抚光腹曰：“咄咄子陵，不可相助为理邪？”
units.en: Yan feigned sleep; Guangwu sat on his couch, patted his belly, and said, "Ziling, Ziling—will you not help me rule?"
units.literal: Guang lay down and did not rise; the emperor came to where he lay, stroked Guang's belly, and said, "Tut-tut, Ziling—can you not assist Us in ordering the realm?"

units.zh: 光又眠不应，良久，乃张目熟视，曰：“昔唐尧著德，巢父洗耳。
units.en: Yan kept his eyes shut, then opened them slowly: "When Yao shone with virtue, Chao Father still washed the taint from his ears.
units.literal: Guang again slept and did not answer; after a long while he then opened his eyes, stared fixedly, and said, "In antiquity Tang Yao displayed virtue, yet Chao Father washed his ears.

units.zh: 士故有志，何至相迫乎！”
units.en: A scholar keeps his own star—why hound him!"
units.literal: Gentlemen therefore have their resolve—how could you press one another!"

units.zh: 帝曰：“子陵，我竟不能下汝邪？”
units.en: Guangwu sighed, "So even I cannot bend you?"
units.literal: The emperor said, "Ziling, am I ultimately unable to make you submit?"

units.zh: 于是升舆叹息而去。
units.en: He climbed into his carriage, sighed, and rode away.
units.literal: Thereupon he mounted the carriage, sighed, and departed.

units.zh: 复引光入，论道旧故，相对累日。
units.en: He brought Yan in again; they talked of the past for days on end.
units.literal: Again he led Guang in and discoursed on the Way and old matters, facing one another for accumulated days.

units.zh: 帝从容问光曰：“朕何如昔时？”
units.en: Once he asked lightly, "How do I measure against my old self?"
units.literal: The emperor leisurely asked Guang, "How do We compare with former times?"

units.zh: 对曰：“陛下差增于往。”
units.en: Yan answered, "You are a bit improved on the young man I knew."
units.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty is a little increased compared with the past."

units.zh: 因共偃卧，光以足加帝腹上。
units.en: They shared a couch; Yan stretched his legs across the emperor's belly.
units.literal: Thereupon they lay down together; Guang placed his foot on the emperor's belly.

units.zh: 明日，太史奏客星犯御坐甚急。
units.en: Next morning the grand astrologer reported a stray star pressing the throne.
units.literal: The next day the grand astrologer reported that a guest star had urgently violated the imperial seat.

units.zh: 帝笑曰：“朕故人严子陵共卧耳。”
units.en: The emperor laughed, "Only my old friend Yan Ziling slept beside me."
units.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "It is merely Our old acquaintance Yan Ziling lying with Us."

units.zh: 除为谏议大夫，不屈，乃耕于富春山，后人名其钓处为严陵濑焉。
units.en: Offered the remonstrance post, he refused and farmed Mount Fuchun; posterity named his fishing pool the Yan Rapids.
units.literal: He was appointed remonstrance official; he would not submit, and therefore plowed on Mount Fuchun; later men named the place where he angled Yanling Rapids.

units.zh: 建武十七年，复特征，不至。
units.en: Jianwu 17 brought another extraordinary summons; he stayed away.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year of Jianwu he was again specially summoned; he did not come.

units.zh: 年八十，终于家。
units.en: He died at home at eighty.
units.literal: At age eighty he ended at home.

units.zh: 帝伤惜之，诏下郡县赐钱百万、谷千斛。
units.en: The emperor mourned and ordered a million cash and a thousand hu of grain for his house.
units.literal: The emperor grieved and pitied him; an edict went down to commanderies and counties to grant a million in cash and a thousand hu of grain.

units.zh: 井丹字大春，扶风郿人也。
units.en: Jing Dan, styled Dachun, came from Mei in Fufeng.
units.literal: Jing Dan, courtesy name Dachun, was a man of Mei in Fufeng.

units.zh: 少受业太学，通《五经》，善谈论，故京师为之语曰：“《五经》纷纶井大春。”
units.en: He studied the Five Classics at the Imperial Academy and shone in debate—hence the capital rhyme: "The Five Classics in glorious tangle—Jing Dachun."
units.literal: In his youth he received instruction at the Imperial Academy, penetrated the Five Classics, and was skilled in discourse; therefore the capital made a saying of him: "The Five Classics in profusion—Jing Dachun."

units.zh: 性清高，未尝修刺候人。
units.en: Proud and aloof, he never paid social calls.
units.literal: By nature he was lofty and pure; he never prepared visiting cards to call on people.

units.zh: 建武末，沛王辅等五王居北宫，皆好宾客，更遣请丹，不能致。
units.en: Late in Jianwu the five princes, including Prince Liu Fu of Pei, lodged in the Northern Palace; all loved hosting guests and in turn sent to invite Jing Dan, but could not bring him.
units.literal: At the end of Jianwu, Prince Liu Fu of Pei and the other five princes dwelt in the Northern Palace; all loved hosting guests and in turn sent to invite Dan, but could not bring him.

units.zh: 信阳侯阴就，光烈皇后弟也，以外戚贵盛，乃诡说五王，求钱千万，约能致丹，而别使人要劫之。
units.en: Yin Jiu, the empress's brother, boasted to the princes for ten million cash that he could deliver Dan—then had him ambushed and dragged in.
units.literal: Marquis Xinyang Yin Jiu, younger brother of the Brilliant Empress, because he was a maternal relative noble and powerful, therefore deceitfully persuaded the five princes, seeking cash to the amount of ten million, agreeing that he could bring Dan about, while separately sending men to intercept and coerce him.

units.zh: 丹不得已，既至，就故为设麦饭葱叶之食。
units.en: Cornered, Jing arrived; Yin served plain wheat porridge and scallions to humiliate him.
units.literal: Dan had no choice; when he had arrived, Jiu purposely for him set out wheat gruel and scallion-leaf food.

units.zh: 丹推去之，曰：“以君侯能供甘旨，故来相过，何其薄乎？”
units.en: Jing pushed the bowl away: "I came thinking a marquis could feast a guest—why this beggar's fare?"
units.literal: Dan pushed it away and said, "Because I thought the lord marquis could supply sweet delicacies, therefore I came to visit you—how is this so meager?"

units.zh: 更置盛馔，乃食。
units.en: Yin laid out a rich table; only then did Jing dine.
units.literal: He again set out a lavish feast, and only then did he eat.

units.zh: 及就起，左右进辇。
units.en: When Yin rose, attendants wheeled up a litter.
units.literal: When Jiu rose, those at his left and right advanced a man-drawn carriage.

units.zh: 丹笑曰：“吾闻桀驾人车，岂此邪？”
units.en: Jing laughed, "I heard Jie of Xia used men for chariots—is this that?"
units.literal: Dan laughed and said, "I have heard that Jie rode men as his carriage—is it this?"

units.zh: 坐中皆失色。
units.en: Every guest blanched.
units.literal: All seated changed color.

units.zh: 就不得已而令去辇。
units.en: Yin had to send the litter off.
units.literal: Jiu had no choice but to order the litter taken away.

units.zh: 自是隐闭，不关人事，以寿终。
units.en: After that he barred his gate to the world and died in old age.
units.literal: From this he hid himself and closed his door, not concerning himself with human affairs, and ended his years by natural lifespan.

units.zh: 梁鸿字伯鸾，扶风平陵人也。
units.en: Liang Hong, styled Boluan, was from Pingling in Fufeng.
units.literal: Liang Hong, courtesy name Boluan, was a man of Pingling in Fufeng.

units.zh: 父让，王莽时为城门校尉，封脩远伯，使奉少昊后，寓于北地而卒。
units.en: His father Liang Rang, under Wang Mang, was colonel of the gates, enfeoffed Baron Xiuyuan to sacrifice to Shaohao, then moved to Beidi and died there.
units.literal: His father Rang, in Wang Mang's time was colonel of the gates, enfeoffed as baron of Xiuyuan, and was sent to continue the line of Shaohao; he lodged in Beidi and died.

units.zh: 鸿时尚幼，以遭乱世，因卷席而葬。
units.en: The boy lived in chaos and buried him with only a mat for coffin.
units.literal: Hong was still young; because he encountered a chaotic age, he therefore rolled up a mat and buried him.

units.zh: 后受业太学，家贫而尚节介，博览无不通，而不为章句。
units.en: Later he studied at the Imperial Academy—poor but principled, widely read, scorning pedantic glosses.
units.literal: Later he received instruction at the Imperial Academy; his family was poor yet he esteemed integrity; he broadly read and there was nothing he did not penetrate, yet he did not do chapter-and-verse analysis.

units.zh: 学毕，乃牧豕于上林苑中。
units.en: When school ended he herded swine in the imperial Shanglin preserve.
units.literal: When his studies were finished, he then herded pigs in the Shanglin Park preserve.

units.zh: 曾误遗火，延及它舍。
units.en: Once he lost a cooking fire that leapt to neighbor huts.
units.literal: Once he mistakenly left a fire, which spread to other houses.

units.zh: 鸿乃寻访烧者，问所去失，悉以豕偿之。
units.en: He tracked every victim, tallied their losses, and paid in pigs.
units.literal: Hong then sought out those burned, asked what they had lost, and fully compensated them with pigs.

units.zh: 其主犹以为少。
units.en: The neighbors still called it insufficient.
units.literal: The owners still thought it too little.

units.zh: 鸿曰：“无它财，愿以身居作。”
units.en: Liang said, "I own nothing else—I will work off the debt with my labor."
units.literal: Hong said, "I have no other wealth; I am willing to dwell and work with my body."

units.zh: 主人许之。
units.en: The landlord agreed.
units.literal: The master of the house granted it.

units.zh: 因为执勤，不懈朝夕。
units.en: He toiled without slack from dawn to dusk.
units.literal: Thereupon because of this he performed labor duties, unremitting morning and evening.

units.zh: 邻家耆老见鸿非恒人，乃共责让主人，而称鸿长者。
units.en: Elders saw he was no common laborer, scolded the landlord, and hailed Liang as a gentleman.
units.literal: The old men of the neighboring village saw that Hong was not an ordinary man; they together reproached the master of the house and praised Hong as an elder.

units.zh: 于是始敬异焉，悉还其豕。
units.en: Ashamed, the landlord returned every pig.
units.literal: Thereupon they began to respect him as extraordinary and wholly returned his pigs.

units.zh: 鸿不受而去，归乡里。
units.en: Liang refused the herd and walked home.
units.literal: Hong would not accept but departed and returned to his home village.

units.zh: 势家慕其高节，多欲女之，鸿并绝不娶。
units.en: Great houses courted him with daughters; he turned down every match.
units.literal: Powerful families admired his lofty integrity and for the most part wished to give him their daughters in marriage; Hong one and all refused and would not marry.

units.zh: 同县孟氏有女，状肥丑而黑，力举石臼，择对不嫁，至年三十。
units.en: A Meng girl in his county—plain, dark, strong enough to hoist a mortar—rejected every suitor until thirty.
units.literal: In the same commandery the Meng family had a daughter, stout, ugly, and dark, who could lift a stone mortar; she chose a mate and would not marry, until age thirty.

units.zh: 父母问其故。
units.en: Her parents asked why.
units.literal: Her parents asked her the reason.

units.zh: 女曰：“欲得贤如梁伯鸾者。”
units.en: She said, "I will marry only a worthy like Liang Boluan."
units.literal: The daughter said, "I wish to obtain a worthy like Liang Boluan."

units.zh: 鸿闻而娉之。
units.en: Liang heard and sent matchmakers.
units.literal: Hong heard and betrothed her.

units.zh: 女求作布衣、麻屦，织作筐缉绩之具。
units.en: She asked only for homespun robes, hemp shoes, loom, basket, and spindle.
units.literal: The daughter asked to make plain cloth garments, hemp sandals, and the tools of weaving, basket-making, and spinning.

units.zh: 及嫁，始以装饰入门。
units.en: On her wedding day she arrived in full paint and silk finery.
units.literal: When she married, only then with adornment did she enter the gate.

units.zh: 七日而鸿不答。
units.en: Liang spoke not a word to her for seven nights.
units.literal: For seven days Hong did not answer her.

units.zh: 妻乃跪床下请曰：“窃闻夫子高义，简斥数妇，妾亦偃蹇数夫矣。
units.en: She knelt by the couch: "I know your honor has sent away many wives; I too have spurned many men.
units.literal: The wife then knelt beneath the bed and requested, saying, "I have heard that the master's lofty righteousness has dismissed several wives; your handmaid also has been proud before several husbands.

units.zh: 今而见择，敢不请罪。”
units.en: Chosen at last, I beg to know my fault."
units.literal: Now that I am chosen, how dare I not beg forgiveness for my offense."

units.zh: 鸿曰：“吾欲裘褐之人，可与俱隐深山者尔。
units.en: Liang answered, "I sought a woman in leather and homespun to vanish with me into the hills.
units.literal: Hong said, "I wanted a person in furs and coarse cloth who could with me hide in the deep mountains—that is all.

units.zh: 今乃衣绮缟，傅粉墨，岂鸿所愿哉？”
units.en: Yet you come painted and robed in gauze—is that what I had in mind?"
units.literal: Now you wear figured silks and apply powder and ink—how could this be what Hong wishes?"

units.zh: 妻曰：“以观夫子之志耳。
units.en: She said, "I dressed to read your heart.
units.literal: The wife said, "It was to observe the master's resolve.

units.zh: 妾自有隐居之服。”
units.en: I keep rough clothes for the life we mean to lead."
units.literal: Your handmaid herself has garments fit for reclusion."

units.zh: 乃更为椎髻，着布衣，操作而前。
units.en: She rebraid her hair, donned homespun, and stepped forward to work.
units.literal: Thereupon she changed to a mallet-shaped hair-knot, put on plain cloth, stepped forward, and worked at the tasks.

units.zh: 鸿大喜曰：“此真梁鸿妻也。
units.en: Liang exulted, "This is the wife of Liang Hong.
units.literal: Hong was greatly pleased and said, "This is truly Liang Hong's wife.

units.zh: 能奉我矣！”
units.en: She can serve my reclusion!"
units.literal: She is able to serve me!"

units.zh: 字之曰德曜，名孟光。
units.en: He gave her the style Deyao—her name was Meng Guang.
units.literal: He styled her Deyao and named her Meng Guang.

units.zh: 居有顷，妻曰：“常闻夫子欲隐居避患，今何为默默？
units.en: Soon she asked, "You always meant to flee the world—why sit idle now?
units.literal: After they had dwelt a while, the wife said, "I have always heard that the master wished to conceal himself and avoid calamity; why are you now silent?

units.zh: 无乃欲低头就之乎？”
units.en: Do you mean to bow and take office after all?"
units.literal: Could it be that you intend to bow your head and accept it?"

units.zh: 鸿曰：“诺。”
units.en: Liang said, "You are right."
units.literal: Hong said, "Agreed."

units.zh: 乃共入霸陵山中，以耕织为业，咏《诗》、《书》，弹琴以自娱。
units.en: Together they fled to Mount Baling, farmed and wove, chanted the Odes and Documents, and played the zither for joy.
units.literal: Thereupon together they entered Mount Baling, took plowing and weaving as their occupation, chanted the Poetry and Documents, and played the zither to amuse themselves.

units.zh: 仰慕前世高士，而为四皓以来二十四人作颂。
units.en: He honored ancient recluses and wrote hymns for twenty-four worthies from the Four Hoaryheads onward.
units.literal: He admired the high gentlemen of former ages and therefore composed encomia for twenty-four men from the Four Elders onward.

units.zh: 因东出关，过京师，作《五噫之歌》曰：“陟彼北芒兮，噫！
units.en: East through the passes he passed Luoyang and sang his "Song of Five Sighs": "I climb the northern ridge—ah!
units.literal: Therefore he went east out of the passes, passed the capital, and composed the "Song of Five Sighs," saying, "I climb that northern mound—yi!

units.zh: 顾览帝京兮，噫！
units.en: I turn and gaze on the royal city—ah!
units.literal: I turn and gaze on the imperial capital—yi!

units.zh: 宫室崔嵬兮，噫！
units.en: Palaces rear against the sky—ah!
units.literal: Palace halls tower—yi!

units.zh: 人之劬劳兮，噫！
units.en: The people labor endless—ah!
units.literal: The toil of men—yi!

units.zh: 辽辽未央兮，噫！”
units.en: Boundless, the palace unending—ah!"
units.literal: Vast, vast, not yet ended—yi!"

units.zh: 肃宗闻而非之，求鸿不得。
units.en: Emperor Zhang heard the song, took offense, and hunted Liang Hong in vain.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhang heard of it he condemned it and sought Hong but could not find him.

units.zh: 乃易姓运期，名耀，字侯光，与妻子居齐鲁之间。
units.en: He therefore changed his surname to Yunqi, his personal name to Yao, and his courtesy name to Houguang, and hid with his wife between Qi and Lu.
units.literal: He therefore changed his surname to Yunqi, his name to Yao, his courtesy name to Houguang, and dwelt with his wife between Qi and Lu.

units.zh: 有顷，又去适吴。
units.en: Soon he moved on toward Wu.
units.literal: Before long he again left and went to Wu.

units.zh: 将行，作诗曰：
units.en: Before leaving he wrote:
units.literal: About to depart, he composed a poem, saying:

units.zh: 逝旧帮兮遐征，将遥集兮东南。
units.en: I quit my homeland for a distant road, bound to roost in the southeast.
units.literal: I leave my old domain on a distant march; I shall aloofly settle in the southeast.

units.zh: 心惙怛兮伤悴，志菲菲兮升降。
units.en: Grief tugs my heart; my purpose flickers high and low.
units.literal: My heart is anxious and wounded; my aims flutter as I rise and fall.

units.zh: 欲乘策兮纵迈，疾吾俗兮作谗。
units.en: I long to ride free, yet loathe a world that trades in malice.
units.literal: I wish to mount the whip and gallop free, yet hate how my folk invent slander.

units.zh: 竞举枉兮措直，咸先佞兮唌々。
units.en: The crooked win office while the upright fall; toadies lead while worthies choke.
units.literal: They vie to raise the crooked and set aside the straight; all put flatterers first and smack their lips.

units.zh: 固靡惭兮独建，冀异州兮尚贤。
units.en: I am not ashamed to stand alone—I trust another land may prize the good.
units.literal: Truly I feel no shame standing alone; I hope in another land they still honor the worthy.

units.zh: 聊逍遥兮遨嬉，缵仲尼兮周流。
units.en: I drift awhile for sport, following Confucius's wide road.
units.literal: For a while I wander and roam, tracing Confucius's circuit round the realm.

units.zh: 倘云睹兮我悦，遂舍车兮即浮。
units.en: If clouds should please me, I will quit the cart and trust myself to the flood.
units.literal: If perchance the clouds should please my eye, I will leave my cart and board a raft at once.

units.zh: 过季札兮延陵，求鲁连兮海隅。
units.en: I call at Jizi's Yanling; I seek Lu Zhonglian on the shore.
units.literal: I pass Jizi at Yanling; I seek Lu Zhonglian by the sea's edge.

units.zh: 虽不察兮光貌，幸神灵兮与休。
units.en: Though I cannot see their faces, the gods at least grant me peace.
units.literal: Though I cannot see their bright faces, happily the spirits grant me rest.

units.zh: 惟季春兮华阜，麦含含兮方秀。
units.en: Late spring on the blooming hill—wheat swelling toward the ear.
units.literal: Only in late spring on the flowering mound, the wheat swelling, just coming into ear.

units.zh: 哀茂时兮逾迈，愍芳香兮日臭。
units.en: I mourn the good years racing by; I pity sweet scent turning stale.
units.literal: I mourn that the lush season hurries past; I pity the fragrance that daily fades.

units.zh: 悼吾心兮不获，长委结兮焉究！
units.en: My heart wins nothing it longs for—this knot—where will it end!
units.literal: I grieve that my heart cannot win its wish; long knotted—where shall it end!

units.zh: 口嚣嚣兮余讪，嗟恇恇兮谁留？
units.en: The crowd mocks my voice; who, trembling, will remain with me?
units.literal: Mouths clamor and mock me; alas, alone, alone—who will stay?

units.zh: 遂至吴，依大家皋伯通，居庑下，为人赁舂。
units.en: He reached Wu, lodged with magnate Gao Botong under the eaves, and earned his keep grinding grain.
units.literal: Thereupon he reached Wu, lodged with the great house of Gao Botong, dwelt beneath the porch gallery, and for people hired out his pestle for grinding.

units.zh: 每归，妻为具食，不敢于鸿前仰视，举案齐眉。
units.en: Each night his wife served supper without lifting her eyes, raising the tray to her brows in respect.
units.literal: Each time he returned, his wife prepared food and did not dare look up before Hong, raising the tray level with her brows.

units.zh: 伯通察而异之，曰：“彼佣能使其妻敬之如此，非凡人也。”
units.en: Gao Botong marveled: "A laborer whose wife honors him so is no common man."
units.literal: Botong observed this and thought it strange, saying, "That hired man can make his wife revere him thus—he is no ordinary person."

units.zh: 乃方舍之于家。
units.en: He moved the couple into his hall.
units.literal: Thereupon he lodged him in his own house.

units.zh: 鴻潛閉著書十餘篇。
units.en: Liang Hong shut himself in and wrote a dozen essays.
units.literal: Hong hid away and closed his door, composing more than ten pieces of writing.

units.zh: 疾且困，告主人曰：“昔延陵季子葬子于嬴博之间，不归乡里，慎勿令我子持丧归去。”
units.en: Dying, he told his host, "When Jizi of Yanling buried his son between Ying and Bo he did not send the corpse home—do not let my son haul my bier back to Fufeng."
units.literal: When he was gravely ill and in distress, he told his host, "In antiquity Jizi of Yanling buried his son between Ying and Bo and did not return him to the home village; take care not to let my son bear the mourning back home."

units.zh: 及卒，伯通等为求葬地于吴要离冢傍。
units.en: At his death Gao and friends buried him beside Yaoli the martyr in Wu.
units.literal: When he died, Botong and others for him sought a burial place beside the tomb of Yaoli in Wu.

units.zh: 咸曰：“要离烈士，而伯鸾清高，可令相近。”
units.en: All agreed: "Yaoli died for honor; Boluan lived in purity—they should lie side by side."
units.literal: All said, "Yaoli was a man of fierce integrity, while Boluan was lofty and pure; it is fitting to let them lie near one another."

units.zh: 葬毕，妻子归扶风。
units.en: When the rites ended, his family went home to Fufeng.
units.literal: When the burial was finished, wife and children returned to Fufeng.

units.zh: 初，鸿友人京兆高恢，少好《老子》，隐于华阴山中。
units.en: His friend Gao Hui of Jingzhao, who loved the Laozi in youth, had hidden on Mount Huayin.
units.literal: In the beginning Hong's friend Gao Hui of Jingzhao, in his youth loved the Laozi and concealed himself in the mountains of Huayin.

units.zh: 及鸿东游思恢，作诗曰：“鸟嘤嘤兮友之期，念高子兮仆怀思，相念恢兮爰集兹。”
units.en: Eastbound, he missed Hui and wrote: "Birds call—friends' season; I long for Gao Zi—my heart dwells here."
units.literal: When Hong roamed east he thought of Hui and composed a poem, saying, "The birds cry softly—the time of friendship; I think of Master Gao—my servant's breast remembers; thinking of Hui—we gather here."

units.zh: 二人遂不复相见。
units.en: They never met again.
units.literal: The two men then never saw each other again.

units.zh: 恢亦高抗，终身不仕。
units.en: Hui stayed proud and never served.
units.literal: Hui likewise was lofty and unbending and to the end of his life did not take office.

units.zh: 高凤字文通，南阳叶人也。
units.en: Gao Feng, styled Wentong, came from Ye in Nanyang.
units.literal: Gao Feng, courtesy name Wentong, was a man of Ye in Nanyang.

units.zh: 少为书生，家以农亩为业，而专精诵读，昼夜不息。
units.en: His family farmed, yet he read day and night without pause.
units.literal: In his youth he was a student; his household took farming as its occupation, yet he devoted himself wholly to recitation, day and night without cease.

units.zh: 妻尝之田，曝麦于庭，令凤护鸡。
units.en: His wife once spread grain in the yard for drying and told him to guard it from hens.
units.literal: His wife once went to the fields, spread wheat in the courtyard, and ordered Feng to watch against chickens.

units.zh: 时天暴雨，而凤持竿诵经，不觉潦水流麦。
units.en: A cloudburst came; Gao stood reciting with his staff until the runoff swept the grain away.
units.literal: At the time heaven sent a violent rain, yet Feng held his staff reciting the classics and did not notice the floodwaters washing away the wheat.

units.zh: 妻还怪问，凤方悟之。
units.en: When she returned and asked, he woke to what had happened.
units.literal: When his wife returned she wondered and questioned him, and only then did Feng realize it.

units.zh: 其后遂为名儒，乃教授于西唐山中。
units.en: He became a renowned teacher in the West Tang hills.
units.literal: After this he became a famous scholar and therefore instructed disciples in the mountains of West Tang.

units.zh: 邻里有争财者，持兵而斗，凤往解之，不已，乃脱巾叩头，固请曰：“仁义逊让，奈何弃之！”
units.en: When neighbors brawled over land with weapons, he intervened; when they would not yield, he tore off his cap, kowtowed, and cried, "Will you throw away humaneness, right, modesty, and yield?"
units.literal: When neighbors quarreled over property, took weapons, and fought, Feng went to reconcile them; they did not stop, so he doffed his headcloth, knocked his head, and earnestly requested, saying, "Humaneness, righteousness, modesty, and yielding—how can you cast them away!"

units.zh: 于是争者怀感，投兵谢罪。
units.en: The fighters dropped their arms, ashamed, and begged pardon.
units.literal: Thereupon the quarrelers felt shame, cast down their weapons, and apologized for their crime.

units.zh: 凤年老，执志不倦，名声著闻。
units.en: In old age he never slackened his purpose; his name spread far.
units.literal: Feng in old age held to his resolve untiringly, and his fame was widely heard.

units.zh: 太守连召请，恐不得免，自言本巫家，不应为吏，又诈与寡嫂讼田，遂不仕。
units.en: The prefect summoned him relentlessly; to escape office he claimed shaman ancestry unfit for clerking and even feuded in court with his widowed sister-in-law over land.
units.literal: The grand administrator repeatedly summoned and invited him; fearing he could not escape obligation, he stated that his family was originally of shamans and was not fit to be a clerk, and also falsely sued his widowed sister-in-law over fields, and therefore did not take office.

units.zh: 建初中，将作大匠任隗举凤直言，到公车，托病逃归。
units.en: Mid-Jianchu the architect Ren Wei nominated him as blunt and upright; he reached the coach office, pleaded sickness, and bolted home.
units.literal: In the middle Jianchu era the court architect Ren Wei recommended Feng for outspoken integrity; he reached the imperial coach office, pleaded illness, and fled home.

units.zh: 推其财产，悉与孤兄子。
units.en: He signed his estate over to his brother's orphan.
units.literal: He pushed aside his property and gave it all to his orphaned elder brother's son.

units.zh: 隐身渔钓，终于家。
units.en: He hid among anglers and died at home.
units.literal: He concealed himself in fishing and angling and ended his years at home.

units.zh: 论曰：先大夫宣侯，尝以讲道余隙，寓乎逸士之篇。
units.en: Comment: My late father, Marquis Xuan, while teaching the Way, set his heart on these tales of recluses.
units.literal: The discussion states: My late father, Marquis Xuan, in the spare moments of expounding the Way, lodged his thoughts in the chapters on withdrawn gentlemen.

units.zh: 至《高文通传》，辍而有感，以为隐者也，因著其行事而论之曰：“古者隐逸，其风尚矣。
units.en: At the Life of Gao Wentong he paused, moved, and judged him a true recluse, then wrote: "Ancient withdrawers set a high tone.
units.literal: When it came to the biography of Gao Wentong, he stopped and felt moved, thinking him a recluse, and therefore set down his deeds and discussed them, saying, "In antiquity those who withdrew had a lofty current.

units.zh: 颍阳洗耳，耻闻禅让；
units.en: At Yingyang they washed their ears, shamed by talk of yielding the throne;
units.literal: At Yingyang they washed their ears, shamed to hear of the abdication;

units.zh: 孤竹长饥，羞食周粟。
units.en: on Mount Guzhu they starved rather than taste Zhou grain.
units.literal: at Guzhu they long hungered, ashamed to eat Zhou grain.

units.zh: 或高栖以违行，或疾物以矫情，虽轨迹异区，其去就一也。
units.en: Some fled aloft to escape the world; some scorned things to steel their purity—different paths, one refusal.
units.literal: Some perched high to flee conduct; some faulted things to temper their purity—though their tracks lay in different regions, their choices of going or staying were one.

units.zh: 若伊人者，志陵青云之上，身晦泥污之下，心名且犹不显，况怨累之为哉！
units.en: Such men aim above the clouds yet hide in the mire—name and heart half-seen—what grudge or bond could snare them?
units.literal: Such men as these— their aims overtop the blue clouds, yet their persons hide in mud and filth; heart and name will hardly show—how much less any web of resentment and entanglement!

units.zh: 与夫委体渊沙，鸣弦揆日者，不其远乎！”
units.en: How far from those who drown themselves or tune a lute to count the days!"
units.literal: Compared with those who yield their bodies to the deep sands and twang their strings while measuring the sun—are they not far removed!"

units.zh: 臺佟字孝威，魏郡鄴人也。
units.en: Tai Tong, styled Xiaowei, came from Ye in Wei commandery.
units.literal: Tai Tong, courtesy name Xiaowei, was a man of Ye in Wei commandery.

units.zh: 隐于武安山，凿穴为居，采药自业。
units.en: He lived in a cave on Mount Wu'an and made his living gathering herbs.
units.literal: He concealed himself on Mount Wu'an, dug a cave for a dwelling, and gathered herbs to support himself.

units.zh: 建初中，州辟，不就。
units.en: Mid-Jianchu the province called him; he stayed away.
units.literal: In the middle Jianchu era the province summoned him; he did not go.

units.zh: 刺史行部，乃使从事致谒。
units.en: When the inspector toured the commandery he sent an aide with a visiting card.
units.literal: When the inspector made his circuit, he then sent an aide to deliver a formal visit.

units.zh: 佟载病往谢。
units.en: Tai rode a sick-cart to apologize.
units.literal: Tong rode in a sickbed cart to decline.

units.zh: 刺史乃执贽见佟曰：“孝威居身如是，甚苦，如何？”
units.en: The inspector brought gifts and said, "Xiaowei, this life is bitter—why endure it?"
units.literal: The inspector then grasped his gift-goods, met Tong, and said, "Xiaowei, to keep your person thus is very bitter—what of it?"

units.zh: 佟曰：“佟幸得保终性命，存神养和。
units.en: Tai answered, "I am lucky to finish my span, nursing spirit in peace.
units.literal: Tong said, "Tong is fortunate enough to preserve life to the end, storing spirit and nurturing harmony.

units.zh: 如明使君奉宣诏书，夕惕庶事，反不苦邪？”
units.en: You who trumpet edicts and lose sleep over every duty—are you not the one in pain?"
units.literal: As for the enlightened envoy who proclaims the edicts of the court and is fearful by night over the myriad tasks—is that not more bitter?"

units.zh: 遂去，隐逸，终不见。
units.en: He left and was never seen again.
units.literal: Thereupon he departed, hid, and to the end was not seen.

units.zh: 韩康字伯休，一名恬休，京兆霸陵人。
units.en: Han Kang, styled Boxiu—also called Tianxiu—was from Baling in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Han Kang, courtesy name Boxiu, also named Tianxiu, was a man of Baling in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 家世著姓。
units.en: His clan was an old great house.
units.literal: His family for generations was a noted surname.

units.zh: 常采药名山，卖于长安市，口不二价，三十余年。
units.en: He gathered drugs on famous peaks and sold them in Chang'an at a fixed price for thirty years.
units.literal: He constantly gathered herbs on famous mountains and sold them in the Chang'an market, never naming two prices, for more than thirty years.

units.zh: 时有女子从康买药，康守价不移。
units.en: A woman tried to haggle; Han would not budge from his price.
units.literal: At the time there was a woman who followed Kang to buy medicine; Kang held to his price and would not shift.

units.zh: 女子怒曰：“公是韩伯休那？
units.en: She snapped, "Are you not Han Boxiu?
units.literal: The woman angrily said, "Sir, are you Han Boxiu?

units.zh: 乃不二价乎？”
units.en: Is that why you never change your price?"
units.literal: Then you will not name two prices?"

units.zh: 康叹曰：“我本欲避名，今小女子皆知有我，何用药为？”
units.en: Han sighed, "I meant to hide my name—now even girls know me—why sell herbs?"
units.literal: Kang sighed and said, "Originally I wished to avoid fame; now even little girls all know there is me—what use have I for medicine?"

units.zh: 乃遁入霸陵山中。
units.en: He vanished into the Baling hills.
units.literal: Thereupon he fled into the Baling mountains.

units.zh: 博士公车连征，不至。
units.en: Erudite office and coach summons piled up unanswered.
units.literal: The erudite office and imperial coach repeatedly summoned him; he did not come.

units.zh: 桓帝乃备玄纁之礼，以安车聘之。
units.en: Emperor Huan sent black silk and a cushioned coach.
units.literal: Emperor Huan then prepared the ritual of dark silk and hired him with a comfortable carriage.

units.zh: 使者奉诏造康，康不得已，乃许诺。
units.en: The envoy cornered him; Han grudgingly agreed.
units.literal: The envoy bearing the edict visited Kang; Kang had no choice and therefore promised.

units.zh: 辞安车，自乘柴车，冒晨先使者发。
units.en: He refused the state coach, hitched a farm cart, and slipped away before dawn ahead of the escort.
units.literal: He declined the comfortable carriage, himself rode a brushwood cart, and before dawn set out ahead of the envoy.

units.zh: 至亭，亭长以韩征君当过，方发人牛修道桥。
units.en: At a relay station the chief, expecting the summoned gentleman, was drafting peasants and oxen to mend the bridge.
units.literal: When he reached the post station, the station chief, because Han the summoned gentleman was about to pass, was just sending men and oxen to repair the road bridge.

units.zh: 及见康柴车幅巾，以为田叟也，使夺其牛。
units.en: Seeing a cart and plain kerchief, he mistook Han for a farmer and seized his ox.
units.literal: When he saw Kang in a brushwood cart with plain headcloth, he thought him an old farmer and ordered men to seize his ox.

units.zh: 康即释驾与之。
units.en: Han unyoked the beast and handed it over.
units.literal: Kang immediately released the harness and gave it to him.

units.zh: 有顷，使者至，知夺牛翁乃征君也。
units.en: Soon the envoy arrived and learned the peasant was the summoned recluse.
units.literal: Before long the envoy arrived, knew that the old man whose ox had been seized was the summoned gentleman.

units.zh: 使者欲奏杀亭长。
units.en: The envoy wanted the station chief executed.
units.literal: The envoy wished to memorialize to execute the station chief.

units.zh: 康曰：“此自老子与之，亭长何罪！”
units.en: Han said, "I gave him the ox myself—what fault is the chief's?"
units.literal: Kang said, "This was something this old man gave him; what crime has the station chief!"

units.zh: 乃止。
units.en: The matter dropped.
units.literal: Thereupon he stopped.

units.zh: 康因中道逃遁，以寿终。
units.en: Han escaped halfway to the capital and died in old age.
units.literal: Kang therefore fled midway on the road and ended his years by natural lifespan.

units.zh: 矫慎字仲彦，扶风茂陵人也。
units.en: Jiao Shen, styled Zhongyan, came from Maoling in Fufeng.
units.literal: Jiao Shen, courtesy name Zhongyan, was a man of Maoling in Fufeng.

units.zh: 少好黄、老，隐遁山谷，因穴为室，仰慕松、乔导引之术。
units.en: In youth he loved Huang-Lao, lived in a cave, and studied the breath arts of the immortals Chisong and Wangzi.
units.literal: In his youth he loved Huang-Lao, concealed himself in mountain valleys, took a cave for a chamber, and admired the arts of guiding and pulling of Chisong and Wangzi.

units.zh: 与马融、苏章乡里并时，融以才博显名，章以廉直称，然皆推先于慎。
units.en: He was Ma Rong's and Su Zhang's contemporary; though Ma won fame for breadth and Su for honesty, both deferred to Shen as their senior.
units.literal: He was of the same village and generation as Ma Rong and Su Zhang; Rong became illustrious through broad talent, Zhang was praised for incorruptibility and uprightness, yet both deferred to Shen as senior.

units.zh: 汝南吴苍甚重之，因遗书以观其志曰：
units.en: Wu Cang of Runan esteemed him and sent this letter to test his mind:
units.literal: Wu Cang of Runan thought very highly of him and therefore sent a letter to observe his intent, saying:

units.zh: 仲彦足下：勤处隐约，虽乘云行泥，栖宿不同，每有西风，何尝不叹！
units.en: Zhongyan, you live hidden while others ride high—whenever the west wind blows I sigh for you.
units.literal: Sir Zhongyan, at your feet: you diligently dwell in obscurity; though one rides clouds and the other walks mud, roosting and lodging differ—whenever the west wind blows, how could I not sigh!

units.zh: 盖闻黄、老之言，乘虚入冥，藏身远遁，亦有理国养人，施于为政。
units.en: Huang-Lao speak of mounting void and hiding far away—yet their teaching can also order states and nurture the people.
units.literal: I have heard the words of Huang and Lao: mounting emptiness and entering darkness, concealing the body and fleeing far—there is also ordering the state and nurturing the people, applied in governing.

units.zh: 至如登山绝迹，神不著其证，人不睹其验。
units.en: But mountaintop exile shows no spirit-sign; no man sees its proof.
units.literal: As for climbing mountains and cutting off tracks, the spirits do not display their verification, and people do not witness their proof.

units.zh: 吾欲先生从其可者，于意何如？
units.en: I urge you to take the workable path—what say you?
units.literal: I wish the master to follow what is feasible in this—what is your thought?

units.zh: 昔伊尹不怀道以待尧、舜之君。
units.en: Yi Yin did not clutch the Way waiting for a Yao or Shun.
units.literal: In antiquity Yi Yin did not hug his doctrine while waiting for a Yao or Shun lord.

units.zh: 方今明明，四海开辟，巢、许无为箕山，夷、齐悔入首阳。
units.en: Today the sage shines and the seas are open—Chao and Xu need not idle on Ji Ridge; Bo and Yi would rue Shouyang.
units.literal: Now the realm is bright and clear, the four seas opened wide; Chao and Xu need not idle on Mount Ji, Bo and Qi would regret entering Mount Shouyang.

units.zh: 足下审能骑龙弄凤，翔嬉云间者，亦非狐兔燕雀所敢谋也。
units.en: If you can ride dragons among the clouds, no fox or sparrow may counsel you.
units.literal: If you, sir, can truly ride dragons and sport with phoenixes, soaring and playing amid the clouds, that is also not something foxes, hares, swallows, and sparrows would dare to plot.

units.zh: 慎不答。
units.en: Jiao never replied.
units.literal: Shen did not answer.

units.zh: 年七十余，竟不肯娶。
units.en: Past seventy he still refused a wife.
units.literal: At over seventy years of age he to the end was unwilling to marry.

units.zh: 后忽归家，自言死日，及期果卒。
units.en: Once he went home, named his death-day, and died on the hour.
units.literal: Later he suddenly returned home, himself stating the day he would die, and when the day came he indeed died.

units.zh: 后人有见慎于敦煌者，故前世异之，或云神仙焉。
units.en: Later witnesses placed him at Dunhuang—some called him a transcendent.
units.literal: Later people saw Shen at Dunhuang; therefore men of former ages thought him strange, and some said he was an immortal.

units.zh: 慎同郡马瑶，隐于汧山，以兔罝为事。
units.en: His townsman Ma Yao hid on Mount Qian and lived by snaring hares.
units.literal: Shen's fellow townsman Ma Yao concealed himself on Mount Qian and took snaring hares as his occupation.

units.zh: 所居俗化，百姓美之，号马牧先生焉。
units.en: His village mended its ways and dubbed him the Horse-Shepherd Master.
units.literal: The vulgar ways where he dwelt were transformed; the common people praised him and styled him Master Horse-Shepherd.

units.zh: 戴良字叔鸾，汝南慎阳人也。
units.en: Dai Liang, styled Shuluan, came from Shenyang in Runan.
units.literal: Dai Liang, courtesy name Shuluan, was a man of Shenyang in Runan.

units.zh: 曾祖父遵，字子高，平帝时，为侍御史。
units.en: His great-grandfather Dai Zun, styled Zigao, served as palace attendant censor under Emperor Ping.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Zun, courtesy name Zigao, under Emperor Ping was palace attendant censor.

units.zh: 王莽篡位，称病归乡里。
units.en: Wang Mang's coup sent him home feigning sickness.
units.literal: When Wang Mang usurped the throne, he pleaded illness and returned to his home village.

units.zh: 家富，好给施，尚侠气，食客常三四百人。
units.en: His clan was rich, open-handed, and chivalrous—three or four hundred retainers sat at his gate.
units.literal: His household was wealthy; he loved to give alms and admired chivalrous spirit; his retainers were constantly three or four hundred men.

units.zh: 时人为之语曰：“关东大豪戴子高。”
units.en: Wits rhymed, "East of the passes the great blade—Dai Zigao."
units.literal: People of the time made a saying of him: "The great stalwart east of the passes—Dai Zigao."

units.zh: 良少诞节，母憙驴鸣，良常学之，以娱乐焉。
units.en: Young Dai Liang flouted small rules: his mother loved donkeys' bray, so he brayed to cheer her.
units.literal: Liang in his youth was unrestrained in propriety; his mother delighted in the braying of donkeys, and Liang often imitated it to amuse her.

units.zh: 及母卒，兄伯鸾居庐啜粥，非礼不行，良独食肉饮酒，哀至乃哭，而二人俱有毁容。
units.en: At her death his brother Boluan took the hut and thin gruel; Dai ate meat and drank wine, wept only when sorrow struck—yet both wasted their faces with grief.
units.literal: When his mother died, his elder brother Boluan dwelt in the mourning hut sipping gruel and would not act contrary to ritual, yet Liang alone ate meat and drank wine, weeping only when grief arrived, yet both had disfigured their appearance.

units.zh: 或问良曰：“子之居丧，礼乎？”
units.en: Critics asked, "Is this mourning by the book?"
units.literal: Someone asked Liang, "Sir, in your dwelling in mourning—is it according to ritual?"

units.zh: 良曰：“然。
units.en: Dai said, "Yes.
units.literal: Liang said, "Yes.

units.zh: 礼所以制情佚也。
units.en: Ritual only reins runaway feeling.
units.literal: Ritual exists in order to regulate emotion when it runs wild.

units.zh: 情苟不佚，何礼之论！
units.en: When feeling never strays, what need of ritual talk!
units.literal: If the emotion does not run wild, what is there to discuss about ritual!

units.zh: 夫食旨不甘，故致毁容之实。
units.en: Fine food tastes ashes—that is how grief hollows the face.
units.literal: To eat delicacies and not find them sweet is what brings the reality of disfiguring the appearance.

units.zh: 若味不存口，食之可也。”
units.en: If your mouth knows no flavor, you may still eat."
units.literal: If flavor is not present in the mouth, eating it is permissible."

units.zh: 论者不能夺之。
units.en: None could answer him.
units.literal: The debaters could not overcome him.

units.zh: 良才既高达，而论议尚奇，多骇流俗。
units.en: His genius was high, his talk outrageous—he shocked the crowd.
units.literal: Liang's talent was already lofty and penetrating, yet his discourse prized the strange and for the most part startled vulgar custom.

units.zh: 同郡谢季孝问曰：“子自视天下孰可为比？”
units.en: His townsman Xie Jixiao asked, "Whom in the empire do you match?"
units.literal: Xie Jixiao of the same commandery asked, "In your own eyes, whom in the realm can compare with you?"

units.zh: 良曰：“我若仲尼长东鲁，大禹出西羌，独步天下，谁与为偶！”
units.en: Dai answered, "Were I Confucius in eastern Lu or Yu rising from the western Qiang, I would walk the world alone—who could pair with me!"
units.literal: Liang said, "If I were Confucius, long in eastern Lu, or Great Yu, coming forth from western Qiang, I would stride alone under heaven—who could be my pair!"

units.zh: 举孝廉，不就。
units.en: Nominated filial and incorrupt, he stayed home.
units.literal: He was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt; he did not go.

units.zh: 再辟司空府，弥年不到，州郡迫之，乃遁辞诣府，悉将妻子，既行在道，因逃入江夏山中。
units.en: Twice the Minister of Works called; he dodged a year, then pretended to comply, marched his family along the road, and bolted into the Jiangxia hills.
units.literal: Twice he was summoned to the Minister of Works office; for a full year he did not arrive; the province and commandery pressed him, and therefore he fabricated an excuse and went to the office, taking along his wife and children; already on the road, he fled into the mountains of Jiangxia.

units.zh: 优游不仕，以寿终。
units.en: He roamed free, never served, and died old.
units.literal: He wandered leisurely and did not take office, and ended his years by natural lifespan.

units.zh: 初，良五女并贤，每有求姻，辄便许嫁，疏裳布被、竹笥木屐以遣之。
units.en: His five daughters were all virtuous; at every match he agreed at once, dowering them with homespun, bamboo boxes, and wooden clogs.
units.literal: In the beginning Liang's five daughters were all worthy; whenever there was a request for marriage, he would at once consent to marry them off, sending them with plain skirts, cloth quilts, bamboo cases, and wooden clogs.

units.zh: 五女能遵其训，皆有隐者之风焉。
units.en: Each daughter kept his teaching and bore a hermit's bearing.
units.literal: The five daughters were able to follow his instructions and all had the air of recluses.

units.zh: 法真字高卿，扶风郿人，南郡太守雄之子也。
units.en: Fa Zhen, styled Gaoqing, was a native of Mei in Fufeng and son of Nan commandery prefect Fa Xiong.
units.literal: Fa Zhen, courtesy name Gaoqing, was a man of Mei in Fufeng, son of Grand Administrator Xiong of Nan commandery.

units.zh: 好学而无常家，博通内外图典，为关西大儒。
units.en: He studied everywhere, mastered inner and outer classics, and became the greatest teacher west of the pass.
units.literal: He loved learning yet had no fixed household; he broadly penetrated inner and outer chart-canons and was the great scholar of the lands west of the pass.

units.zh: 弟子自远方至者，陈留范冉等数百人。
units.en: Hundreds of pupils—Fan Ran of Chenliu among them—trekked to his door.
units.literal: Disciples who came from distant regions included several hundred such as Fan Ran of Chenliu.

units.zh: 性恬静寡欲，不交人间事。
units.en: Calm and desireless, he shunned the world's traffic.
units.literal: By nature he was quiet, tranquil, and of few desires; he did not mingle in human affairs.

units.zh: 太守请见之，真乃幅巾诣谒。
units.en: The prefect asked an audience; Fa came in plain kerchief.
units.literal: The grand administrator requested to see him; Zhen then in plain headcloth went to pay a visit.

units.zh: 太守曰：“昔鲁哀公虽为不肖，而仲尼称臣。
units.en: The prefect said, "Duke Ai of Lu was no sage, yet Confucius called himself his minister.
units.literal: The grand administrator said, "In antiquity Duke Ai of Lu, though unworthy, yet Confucius called himself his subject.

units.zh: 太守虚薄，欲以功曹相屈，光赞本朝，何如？”
units.en: I am a shallow man—I would name you merit clerk to help the throne—will you?"
units.literal: I, the grand administrator, am empty and thin; I wish to bend you to the post of merit clerk, to brighten and assist this court—what do you say?"

units.zh: 真曰：“以明府见待有礼，故敢自同宾末。
units.en: Fa answered, "You receive me with courtesy, so I may sit as a guest.
units.literal: Zhen said, "Because the enlightened lord has treated me with ritual, I dare align myself with the least of guests.

units.zh: 若欲吏之，真将在北山之北，南山之南矣。”
units.en: Make me a clerk and you will find me north of North Mountain or south of South Mountain—gone."
units.literal: If you wish to make me a clerk, Zhen will be north of North Mountain, south of South Mountain."

units.zh: 太守戄然，不敢复言。
units.en: The prefect blanched and said no more.
units.literal: The grand administrator was shaken and did not dare speak again.

units.zh: 辟公府，举贤良，皆不就。
units.en: Summons from the high ministers and worthy nominations alike went unanswered.
units.literal: He was summoned to the duke's office and recommended as worthy and good; in neither case did he go.

units.zh: 同郡田弱荐真曰：“处士法真，体兼四业，学穷典奥，幽居恬泊，乐以忘忧。
units.en: Tian Ruo wrote: "Fa Zhen unites the four callings, plumbs the classics, lives hidden in joy, and forgets sorrow.
units.literal: Tian Ruo of the same commandery recommended Zhen, saying, "The gentleman Fa Zhen embodies the four occupations, his learning exhausts the canons' depths, he dwells in seclusion quiet and still, and joy makes him forget care.

units.zh: 将蹈老氏之高踪，不为玄纁屈也。
units.en: He will follow Laozi's high path and spurn imperial silk.
units.literal: He will tread the lofty tracks of Laozi and will not bend for dark silk.

units.zh: 臣愿圣朝就加衮职，必能唱《清庙》之歌，致来仪之凤矣。”
units.en: Add him to the high ministers and he will lead the Clear Temple hymn and summon the phoenix of peace."
units.literal: Your servant wishes the sage court to add him to the corded and embroidered ranks—he will surely be able to lead the Clear Temple hymn and bring the phoenix of auspicious arrival."

units.zh: 会顺帝西巡，弱又荐之。
units.en: When Emperor Shun toured the west, Tian Ruo recommended him again.
units.literal: It happened that Emperor Shun was touring west; Ruo again recommended him.

units.zh: 帝虚心欲致，前后四征。
units.en: The emperor emptied his pride and summoned him four times.
units.literal: The emperor with humble mind wished to obtain him and summoned him four times in succession.

units.zh: 真曰：“吾既不能遁形远世，岂饮洗耳之水哉？”
units.en: Fa said, "I cannot vanish like a ghost—shall I then mimic ear-washing hermits?"
units.literal: Zhen said, "Since I am unable to conceal my form and flee the world, how could I drink the water of ear-washing?"

units.zh: 遂深自隐绝，终不降屈。
units.en: He buried himself deeper and never bowed.
units.literal: Thereupon he deeply hid himself and cut off contact, and to the end did not submit.

units.zh: 友人郭正称之曰：“法真名可得闻，身难得而见，逃名而名我随，避名而名我追，可谓百世之师者矣！”
units.en: Guo Zheng said, "You hear Fa Zhen's name but never see the man—shun fame and it hunts you—he is a teacher for ages!"
units.literal: His friend Guo Zheng praised him, saying, "Fa Zhen's name can be heard, yet his person is hard to obtain and see; he flees fame and fame follows me; he avoids fame and fame pursues me—he may be called a teacher for a hundred generations!"

units.zh: 乃共刊石颂之，号曰玄德先生。
units.en: They carved a stone ode and named him Master Profound Virtue.
